text:
rachael_finance: Heads-up team — starting June 1 were updating vendor onboarding and AP cutoffs to speed payments and reduce manual follow-ups. Key items below and a short checklist in the vendor portal: https://redwood.app/finance/vendor-onboard :loud_sound:
sam_ops: What are the biggest changes?
rachael_finance: Short list: 1) Standard vendors (expected annual spend < $20k and standard T&Cs) can be auto-approved in 48h if the intake form + W-9 (or equivalent) + bank remittance details are provided. 2) Payment terms default to Net-30 for auto-approved vendors (was Net-45). 3) Vendors must submit invoices via AP portal within 90 days of invoice date or they may be declined. 4) Any vendor accessing PII or with expected spend > $50k requires security review (SOC2 or completed security questionnaire) and manual legal review.
noah_vendor: We're a small analytics vendor — assumed we'd keep Net-45. Net-30 will be tight for our cashflow. Any flexibility?
rachael_finance: We expect smaller vendors to be fine with Net-30; if not, they can opt for early-pay at a 1% fee or request Net-45 during vendor setup (requires manager approval). Were trying to reduce days payable outstanding and improve predictability.
amy_accounting: FYI for PO/request workflow: procurement will create PO for approved vendors and attach remittance instructions. AP will only process invoices that match a PO or have an approved exception. Exceptions should use the "Invoice Exception" form in the portal.
procure-bot: New rules live: `VendorIntake > AutoApprove48h`, `AP > InvoiceCutoff90d`, `Payments > DefaultNet30`. Missing remittance or tax docs auto-flag vendor for manual review.
sam_ops: For existing vendors, do we need to re-submit docs or will procurement reach out? We have some older partners on file.
rachael_finance: Procurement will run a 30-day cleanup. Vendors without W-9/bank info will receive an automated request to update their profile. If they don't respond, payments will be held until the record is complete. We'll post a list of at-risk vendors in the portal.
noah_vendor: About the security review: we already have a SOC2 report but its older than a year. Is that ok?
rachael_finance: Acceptable if it's within 15 months; otherwise vendor should provide the most recent. If a vendor can't provide SOC2, they can complete our 12-point security questionnaire and provide evidence. Legal will triage edge cases.
amy_accounting: Quick note on invoices: AP prefers PDFs with the following fields: vendor name, invoice number, date, PO number (if applicable), line-item breakdown, and remittance instructions. Invoices missing a PO will need the "Invoice Exception" field filled by the owner.
procure-bot: Reminder: tag new vendors with `#owner`, `#cost-center`, and `#tax-class` in intake form. Missing tags = manual review.
sam_ops: Are there any new SLAs for procurement response times on manual reviews?
rachael_finance: Manual review SLA: procurement aims for 5 business days for standard manual reviews, 10-15 days if legal/security review is required. If you need faster turnaround, use the "expedite" checkbox and justify urgency.
oah_vendor: Good to know. One last Q  can vendors request ACH vs virtual card?
amy_accounting: Both supported. ACH is preferred for recurring payouts. Virtual cards will still be used for one-off purchases and for teams that requested them. ACH setup requires bank account + voided check or bank letter during intake.
sam_ops: Can you post a one-line checklist for our vendor onboarding doc?
rachael_finance: Done in the portal guide. TL;DR: 1) Complete vendor intake form 2) Attach W-9 (or tax equiv) + bank remittance 3) Indicate owner, cost-center, and expected annual spend 4) Attach SOC2 or complete security questionnaire if handling PII 5) Choose payment terms (Net-30 default) or request exception.
procure-bot: Audit note: procurement will run a 60-day audit on migrated vendors and publish a findings summary to #finance.
noah_vendor: Thanks all, we'll update our intake today.
rachael_finance: Thanks! Ping vendor-ops@redwood.com for weird edge cases. We'll monitor the first 60 days and iterate. :seedling:
